body:
Add item was a floating AlertDialog. Three problems on the screen reached most often
in the app:

1. Opening it left the Name field unfocused, so adding an item took an extra tap
   before you could type.
2. The soft keyboard covered Add and Cancel -- adding one item meant dismissing the
   keyboard first to reach the button.
3. It looked and behaved unlike Edit item, which had already been made full-screen
   for exactly reason 2 (T-80).

Fix: rebuild Add item on the same full-screen layout as Edit item -- fixed header,
scrolling field area, fixed action bar, decorFitsSystemWindows(false) so the IME is a
real inset. Focus Name on open after a frame wait (the dialog is its own window; a
focus request issued before that window exists is dropped, and the keyboard with it).

Also drops "Add another" at the user's request, so the two dialogs match: Cancel then
the primary action. That removes ItemFormViewModel.saveAndAddAnother, the closeAfter
parameter, ItemFormUiState.focusNameSignal, the T-41 test, and item_add_another from
all nine locales.

Note: the web client keeps its own "Add another" (ItemDialog.tsx), so the clients
deliberately diverge here for now.
title: Android: Add-item dialog needs a tap to focus and hides its buttons behind the keyboard
